claims.text: A 5-year-old boy with distal hypospadias was brought to the emergency department with a 14-hour history of urinary difficulty, passing urine only in small drops without associated pain, after three self-resolved similar episodes in the past year. Examination showed a small stenotic sub-coronal meatus; urinalysis and culture showed infection with coagulase-negative Staphylococcus species, and ultrasound showed a thick-walled bladder with layering debris and no calculi. Family history included distal hypospadias in the father.

claims.text: He was discharged on cephalexin and later attended outpatient follow-up, after which surgical repair was planned. On the day of surgery five weeks later his mother reported additional episodes with manual expression of small stones, and a small stone was found at the stenotic meatus during a tubularized-incised plate hypospadias repair with a 5 Fr urethral catheter. He had abdominal pain and peri-catheter leakage on postoperative day 1, resolved by flushing and aspirating the catheter. The catheter was removed on postoperative day 11, and at follow-up the meatus was orthotopic of normal caliber, he was voiding normally and the parents reported no further episodes.
